questions.question: The combination of high levels of which type of fats with low HDL cholesterol or high LDL cholesterol levels can increase the risk of heart attack and stroke?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Triglycerides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Triglycerides** are a type of fat (lipid) found in your blood, primarily derived from calories consumed that are not immediately used by the body.
 
• High levels of triglycerides in the blood, when combined with low HDL (good cholesterol) or high LDL (bad cholesterol), significantly increase the risk of **heart attack, stroke, and cardiovascular disease.**
 
• Normal triglyceride levels are below **150 mg/dL**; levels above 200 mg/dL are considered high and pose health risks.
 
• Common causes of high triglyceride levels include **obesity, uncontrolled diabetes, excessive alcohol consumption, and high-calorie diets.**
 
• Maintaining a healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise, a balanced diet, and avoiding smoking, can help manage triglyceride levels effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **LDL (Low-Density Lipoprotein):**

 
 
• Known as "bad cholesterol," LDL carries cholesterol to the arteries, where it can form plaques and lead to blockages.
 
• High levels of LDL are a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases such as heart attack and stroke.
 
• Recommended LDL levels are below 100 mg/dL for optimal heart health.
 
 
 
• **HDL (High-Density Lipoprotein):**
 
 
• Known as "good cholesterol," HDL helps remove excess cholesterol from the bloodstream, transporting it to the liver for excretion.
 
• Higher levels of HDL are associated with reduced risk of heart disease.
 
• Healthy HDL levels are 60 mg/dL or higher.
 
 
 
• **Triglycerides vs Cholesterol:**
 
 
• Triglycerides store unused calories and provide energy, whereas cholesterol is used to build cells and hormones.
 
• Both are lipids, but they serve different functions in the body.
 
 
 
• **Preventive Measures for High Lipid Levels:**
 
 
• Adopt a diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins while avoiding trans fats and sugary foods.
 
• Engage in regular aerobic exercise to improve lipid profiles and overall heart health.
 
• Limit alcohol intake and quit smoking to reduce triglyceride levels and improve HDL levels.

questions.question: Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan was introduced by the Government of India in how many states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan (GKRA) was launched by the Government of India on **20 June 2020** to boost livelihood opportunities for migrant workers.
 
• This program was implemented in **six states**: Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Odisha, and Jharkhand.
 
• It was initiated as a **125-day campaign** to address the economic distress caused by the reverse migration of workers due to the COVID-19 lockdown.
 
• The program aimed to provide **employment opportunities** in rural areas by utilizing the existing skill sets of migrant workers.
 
• A total of **25 target-driven schemes** from 12 ministries were combined under GKRA, with an allocation of Rs. 50,000 crores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Targeted States**

 
 
• The six states were chosen based on the large number of returning migrant workers during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• Bihar had the highest number of districts (32) under the campaign, followed by Uttar Pradesh (31 districts).
 
 
 
• **Focus Areas**
 
 
• The campaign focused on rural infrastructure development such as roads, housing, community centers, and water conservation projects.
 
• It also promoted skill development and self-reliance initiatives under the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan.
 
 
 
• **Execution and Monitoring**
 
 
• The program was implemented in a coordinated effort by the central and state governments.
 
• It was monitored through a technology-driven platform to ensure transparency and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Impact and Outcomes**
 
 
• Over 50 crore person-days of employment were generated by the end of the campaign.
 
• The initiative helped stabilize rural economies during the pandemic by creating job opportunities at the local level.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees equality before the law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 14** of the Indian Constitution guarantees **equality before the law** and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• This article ensures that no person is above the law and emphasizes that laws should be applied uniformly, irrespective of an individual's status.
 
• It is a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution, promoting the principle of **rule of law**.
 
• The concept of "equality before the law" originates from the British legal system, while "equal protection of the laws" is inspired by the U.S. Constitution.
 
• This article forms the cornerstone of India's commitment to secularism, non-discrimination, and justice in a democratic setup.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equality before the law:**

 
 
• This concept originates from the rule of law propounded by A.V. Dicey in England.
 
• It means that no individual, regardless of their rank or position, is exempt from the jurisdiction of the ordinary courts.
 
• It prevents any special privileges for individuals or groups under the law.
 
 
 
• **Equal protection of the laws:**
 
 
• This phrase is derived from the 14th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution.
 
• It mandates that individuals in similar circumstances will be treated equally by the law.
 
• However, reasonable classification (not arbitrary) is permitted under this principle.
 
 
 
• **Doctrine of Reasonable Classification:**
 
 
• The state can make laws that apply differently to different groups, provided the classification is reasonable.
 
• It must fulfill two criteria: (i) Classification must be based on intelligible differentia, and (ii) It must have a rational nexus with the object of the law.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights under Part III:**
 
 
• Articles 12–35 of the Indian Constitution enumerate the Fundamental Rights available to citizens.
 
• These rights are enforceable by courts and aim to protect individual freedoms and uphold equality.
 
 
 
• **Exceptions to Article 14:**
 
 
• The President and Governors enjoy certain immunities under Articles 361 and 361A.
 
• Diplomatic immunity is provided to foreign diplomats under international law.

questions.question: A player/team needs to win two consecutive points immediately after '__________' to win the game as per the International Tennis Federation norms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**deuce**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In tennis, a **deuce** occurs when both players or teams reach a score of 40-all (three points each).
 
• To win the game after a deuce, a player/team must win **two consecutive points**.
 
• The first point won after deuce is called an **advantage**, indicating that the player/team is one point away from winning the game.
 
• If the player/team with the advantage loses the next point, the score returns to **deuce**, and the cycle continues.
 
• This scoring rule ensures that players must earn a decisive two-point lead to win a game after deuce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Love:**

 
 
• In tennis, **love** refers to a score of zero.
 
• The term is derived from the French word "l'œuf," meaning "egg," which symbolizes zero.
 
 
 
• **Set:**
 
 
• A **set** in tennis consists of games won by a player/team.
 
• A player/team typically needs to win **six games** with a margin of at least two games to win a set.
 
 
 
• **Advantage:**
 
 
• Advantage refers to the point immediately following deuce, where a player/team is one point away from winning the game.
 
• If the player/team with the advantage loses the next point, the score returns to deuce.
 
 
 
• **International Tennis Federation (ITF):**
 
 
• The ITF is the governing body for world tennis, overseeing international tournaments and establishing rules.
 
• It was founded in 1913 and manages key events such as the Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup.

questions.question: Which is the most fascinating and unique festival of Assam where the system of quid pro quo comes alive?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Junbeel Mela is a unique and traditional festival of Assam, which is held every year in the third week of January.
 
• This festival is celebrated by the community of Tiwa tribe and it showcases an ancient reciprocal system.
 
• In Junbeel Mela, people exchange goods through barter system, in which modern currency is not used.
 
• This fair is held in Morigaon district and apart from the Tiwa community, other tribes also participate in it.
 
• Junbeel Mela is not only a platform for trade but also cultural programs, traditional dance and music are organized.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tiwa tribe**

 
 
• The Tiwa tribe is an important tribe of Assam and Meghalaya.
 
• They are also known as "Lalung" and the barter system has a special place in their culture.
 
 
 
• **Barter system **
 
 
• It is an age old trade system in which goods and services are exchanged without currency.
 
• Junbeel Mela is a living example of barter system.
 
 
 
• **Other major festivals of Assam**
 
 
• Bhogali Bihu: Harvest festival.
 
• Ambubachi Mela: A religious fair held at Kamakhya temple.
 
• Rangali Bihu: The biggest and colourful festival of Assam.
 
 
 
• **Name of junbil**
 
 
• The name Junbeel is derived from "jun" (moon) and "beel" (lake), as the fair is held near a crescent-shaped lake.

questions.question: In which of the following Buddhist texts are the rules mentioned for Buddhist monks and nuns?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinaya Pitaka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vinaya Pitaka** is one of the three baskets (Tripitaka) of Buddhist scriptures that contains the rules and regulations for monks and nuns within the Buddhist monastic community (Sangha).
 
• The text provides detailed guidance on monastic discipline, including codes of conduct, procedures for resolving disputes, and penalties for violations.
 
• The Vinaya Pitaka is divided into three main parts: **Sutta Vibhanga** (rules for individual monks and nuns), **Khandhaka** (procedural rules for the Sangha), and **Parivara** (a summary and analysis of rules).
 
• It was compiled during the First Buddhist Council held at Rajgir (Rajagriha) shortly after Buddha’s death (parinirvana) to preserve the monastic traditions and teachings.
 
• The Vinaya Pitaka serves as a cornerstone for maintaining the moral and ethical framework of the Buddhist monastic community, ensuring harmony and discipline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tripitaka (Three Baskets):**

 
 
• The Tripitaka consists of three main texts: Vinaya Pitaka (discipline), Sutta Pitaka (teachings), and Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical analysis).
 
• It forms the canonical literature of Theravada Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Sutta Pitaka:**
 
 
• It is a collection of discourses delivered by Buddha and his close disciples.
 
• The Sutta Pitaka focuses on ethical teachings and philosophical concepts.
 
 
 
• **Abhidhamma Pitaka:**
 
 
• This text contains a detailed analysis of Buddhist doctrines and concepts.
 
• It is considered an advanced and systematic elaboration of Buddha's teachings.
 
 
 
• **Role of Monastic Rules:**
 
 
• The rules in the Vinaya Pitaka ensure discipline, ethical conduct, and spiritual growth among monks and nuns.
 
• Adherence to these rules fosters a harmonious and conducive environment for practicing the Dhamma.

questions.question: Which industry type is involved in activities like farming, fishing and forestry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Primary industry** involves activities that extract natural resources directly from the Earth, such as farming, fishing, forestry, and mining.
 
• These industries are the foundation of the economy, as they provide raw materials for other industries like manufacturing and construction.
 
• Examples include agriculture, where crops are grown; forestry, which involves harvesting wood; and fishing, which supplies seafood for consumption.
 
• Primary industries are typically labor-intensive and depend heavily on natural factors such as climate, soil quality, and water availability.

• **Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956:**

questions.question: If the government decides to privatise a major public sector industry, what might be an unintended consequence?

__
 
• Privatisation of major public sector industries can lead to the concentration of ownership and control in a few private entities, increasing the likelihood of monopolistic practices.
 
• Monopolistic behavior may result in price manipulation, reduced competition, and exploitation of consumers due to the absence of sufficient market regulation.
 
• Essential services provided by the industry may become less accessible or unaffordable for economically weaker sections of society.
 
• Government oversight may diminish after privatisation, making it harder to enforce regulations to prevent monopolistic tendencies.
 
• In the absence of adequate checks, the industry may prioritize profit over public welfare, negatively impacting service quality and equitable resource allocation.

• Its main objectives include enhancing operational efficiency, reducing fiscal burden, and encouraging private investment.
 
 
 
• **Monopoly:**
 
 
• A monopoly exists when a single entity dominates the market, with little or no competition.
 
• Monopolies can lead to higher prices, reduced innovation, and limited consumer choices.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Oversight:**
 
 
• Regulatory bodies like the Competition Commission of India (CCI) are tasked with ensuring fair practices and curbing monopolistic behavior.
 
• Privatisation may require stronger regulatory frameworks to balance profit motives with public interest.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Privatisation can boost economic growth by attracting private investment and enhancing operational efficiency.
 
• However, unchecked privatisation may lead to negative externalities, such as income inequality and reduced access to essential services.

questions.question: In an experiment, the refractive index of water was found to be 1.35, 1.29, 1.32 and 1.36. What is the average refractive index of water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Deviation Method for Averages

If an assumed mean A is taken, the actual mean = A + (Sum of deviations ÷ Total number of items). This drastically reduces calculation effort for closely grouped numbers.

Combined Average

If group 1 has n₁ items with average A₁ and group 2 has n₂ items with average A₂, the combined average is calculated as: (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

The refractive index (n) is a dimensionless number describing how fast light travels through a material. It is calculated as the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in the medium (n = c ÷ v). The standard refractive index of water is approximately 1.33.

questions.question: A can complete a task in 16 days, and B can complete the same task in 24 days. If A and B work on alternate days starting with A, in how many days will the task be completed?

Efficiency of A = 3 units/day, Efficiency of B = 2 units/day.

Work done in 2 days (A then B) = 3 + 2 = 5 units.

In 18 days (9 cycles), work done = 9 × 5 = 45 units.

Remaining 3 units are completed by A on the 19th day (3 ÷ 3 = 1 day).

**∴ The correct answer is 19 days.**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in the first 2 days (1 cycle) = 3 (by A) + 2 (by B) = 5 units

questions.question: The LCM of 16, 45, 135 and 144 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The LCM must be exactly divisible by all the given numbers: 16, 45, 135, and 144.

Since 144 is a multiple of 9 (144 = 16 × 9), the LCM must also be a multiple of 9.

Checking the sum of digits of the given options for divisibility by 9:

Only 2160 has a digit sum of 9 (2 + 1 + 6 + 0 = 9), which means it is completely divisible by 9.

It also ends in a 0, satisfying the divisibility criteria for both 5 (from 45) and an even number (from 16).

**∴ The correct answer is 2160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers to find the LCM for are 16, 45, 135, and 144.

**Method Used: Prime Factorisation**

⇒ Prime factors of 16 = 2⁴

⇒ Prime factors of 45 = 3² × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 135 = 3³ × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 144 = 2⁴ × 3²

The LCM is evaluated by taking the product of the highest powers of all prime factors present in the numbers.

⇒ Highest power of 2 = 2⁴

⇒ Highest power of 3 = 3³

⇒ Highest power of 5 = 5¹

⇒ LCM = 2⁴ × 3³ × 5

⇒ LCM = 16 × 27 × 5

⇒ LCM = 16 × 135

⇒ LCM = 2160

**∴ The correct answer is 2160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is completely divisible by each of the given numbers. It is determined by taking the highest power of each unique prime factor involved.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is exactly divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 9. This simple trick is extremely useful for quickly eliminating options in complex LCM calculations.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two specific numbers a and b, their product is exactly equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. Formula: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b). Note that this specific rule does not directly apply to three or more numbers.
</p
